thread:
alex: Escalation from AcmeOps. Customer sees partial SSE events after client reconnects through a gRPC-web -> gateway -> backend path. They say stream resumes but last event is truncated. First report 14:02 UTC. Attach: repro steps + logs.

maria: thanks — can you paste the minimal repro and a trace link? pinging @jack for runtime. :eyes:

alex: Repro (simplified):
```
# client uses gRPC-web (h2) -> gateway (translates to h1) -> backend SSE
curl --http2-prior-knowledge -N "https://gw.example/acme/stream" -H "Accept: text/event-stream"
```
Observed: on reconnect, client receives a partial event payload (no trailing "\n\n"), then stream cuts. Gateway logs show a 502/connection reset on the backend shortly after.

jack: I've seen variants of this. Gateway may be coalescing small h2 DATA frames into a single chunk for h1, so if the backend closes mid-coalesced-chunk we emit a partial chunk. Client reconnects, thinks last event wasn't completed. Does Acme use any intermediate caching or NLB?

alex: They have CloudLB + an Nginx sidecar in front of the backend. No caching. I've attached gw and backend logs snippet: "upstream prematurely closed connection while sending request to client" + repeated \"writev: broken pipe\" entries.

luis: quick test idea: try forcing chunked boundaries per h2 DATA frame on the gateway, and disable proxy_buffering in nginx. Also test with `curl -N --http2` vs `curl -N --http1.1` to compare behavior.

sam: customer is also worried about billing — they said tokens seemed double-counted on reconnect. Can we confirm whether we retry on our side or the client replayed messages?

jack: likely the client replayed the request on reconnect, but token accounting should only count accepted bytes at the runtime. I'll check request-id propagation.

maria: @infra-bot can you pull the trace from 2026-03-15 14:02 UTC for request id acme-req-4773?

infra-bot: trace: https://traces.internal/trace/acme-req-4773 (collected spans: gateway->nginx->backend). Observed gap: gateway emitted single 16KB h1 chunk, backend sent two 8KB h2 DATA frames; backend closed after second frame while gateway still streaming.

jack: repro on our dev infra: h2->h1 proxy coalesces frames by default. When backend closes mid-chunk, gateway forwarded incomplete chunk and closed connection. Client receives truncated SSE event. Reconnect flow: client posts new request; backend treats it as fresh, so tokens may be charged again.

luis: proposed mitigation: change gateway to flush per h2 DATA frame as separate h1 chunk (no coalescing), or preserve DATA boundaries by streaming small frames with proper CRLF separators. Also ensure server emits event delimiters (`\n\n`) before connection close when possible.

jack: short-term canary: disabled h2->h1 chunk coalescing on canary gateway in us-west-2. deploy-bot rolled canary id dg-3098 to 10% traffic.

deploy-bot: rollout dg-3098 -> canary 10% -> started 14:48 UTC.

sam: communicated mitigation steps to Acme; asked them to retry after 15 minutes and report whether truncation persists. Also escalated billing question to finance ops.

maria: notes for oncall: check token accounting for acme-req-4773 and similar ids; confirm no duplicate billing after canary. If canary fixes repro, schedule full rollout and a patch to never coalesce if streaming SSE.

jack: root cause summary: intermediary (gateway) coalesced h2 DATA frames into larger h1 chunk; when backend closed mid-chunk we forwarded a partial chunk, leaving client with incomplete SSE event. Reconnect caused request replays -> perceived double billing. Fix path: preserve DATA boundaries or ensure graceful event termination before close. Patch PR incoming. :thumbsup:

alex: thanks everyone, assigning follow-ups. I'll keep Acme updated.
